extracted.intended_audience: Far West spearmint oil producers, handlers, industry stakeholders, and members of the public who may submit comments on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: A USDA/AMS proposed rule establishing salable quantities and allotment percentages for Class 1 (Scotch) and Class 3 (Native) Far West spearmint oil for the 2025-2026 marketing year, including the Committee's basis for recommendations and related procedural and analytic requirements. The page describes definitions, computations, data inputs, statutory/administrative authorities, and how interested persons may comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received by October 27, 2025 and should be submitted to the Docket Clerk, Market Development Division, Specialty Crops Program, AMS, USDA (mail), by Email: MarketingOrderComment@usda.gov, or via https://www.regulations.gov. Comments should reference the document number and the date and page number of this issue of the Federal Register. Comments submitted will be included in the record and made available to the public; the identity of commenters will be made public and Agencies may redact or withhold certain submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within stated deadline; include document number and FR citation; comments become part of public record and may be redacted/withheld by the agency; one comment already received on Regulations.gov for this docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and administrative authority for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is proposed pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553 and Marketing Order No. 985 (7 CFR part 985), under the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937 (7 U.S.C. 601-674). The proposed rule is reviewed under Executive Orders 12866 and 13563, Executive Order 13175, and Executive Order 12988 with stated findings on OMB review exemption and tribal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider cost/benefit and other Executive Order requirements (quantifying costs/benefits, reducing costs, harmonizing rules, promoting flexibility). Note references to specific statutory sections (§§ 985.50, 985.51, § 608c(15)(A) of the Act) that establish procedural rights and administrative remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors Committee considers when recommending volume regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining marketing policy and recommending salable quantities and allotment percentages, the Committee considers current and projected supply of oil, estimated future demand, production costs, producer prices for each class, input from handlers and producers, established acreage, consumer demand, existing carry-in, reserve pool volume, production in competing markets, historical sales, inventory statistics, and international market data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee uses these factors to ensure market requirements are satisfied and orderly marketing conditions maintained; recommendations are made in advance to allow producers time to adjust production decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of salable quantity and allotment percentage
rubrics_metrics.description: Salable quantity represents the total quantity of each class of oil which handlers may purchase from, or handle on behalf of, producers during a given marketing year. The allotment percentage for each class is the salable quantity for that class divided by the total of all producers' allotment base for the same class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute annual producer allotments by multiplying a producer's allotment base by the allotment percentage; example numeric computations provided for Scotch and Native classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer allotment base and annual revision
rubrics_metrics.description: A producer's allotment base is their calculated share of the spearmint oil market based on a statistical representation of their past spearmint production and sales. The Committee periodically reviews and adjusts each producer's allotment base in accordance with a formula prescribed by the Committee and approved by AMS, revised each year on June 1 (§ 985.53 references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allotment base adjustments account for the 'bona fide effort' production provision (§ 985.53(e)) and additional base made available pursuant to § 985.153; total estimated allotment base is used to compute the salable quantity when multiplied by the recommended allotment percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of minimum required salable quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum salable quantity is calculated by subtracting estimated salable carry-in on June 1 from the estimated trade demand for the marketing year (i.e., minimum amount required from the current year's production to meet estimated demand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee provides worked examples: Scotch minimum salable quantity = 645,000 (trade demand) - 25,880 (carry-in) = 619,120 pounds; Native similarly computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discretion to adjust computed allotment percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee may recommend an allotment percentage different from the computed percentage (minimum salable quantity divided by total allotment base) based on input from producers and handlers and to ensure adequate supply and desirable carry-in levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: computed Scotch percentage was 26.8 percent but Committee recommended 35 percent after deliberation and stakeholder input to better supply anticipated demand and carry-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-seasonal increase authority and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Order (§ 985.51), the Committee has authority to recommend intra-seasonal increases to the salable quantity and allotment percentage if market conditions indicate the initially established levels are insufficient to supply demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve pool oil is not available after December 1 in the current marketing year without an increase; reserve oil may also be released for limited market development projects with Secretary approval (rarely used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Salable carry-in and reserve pool definitions and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Salable carry-in represents overproduction from prior years available to the market without restriction. Reserve pool oil is produced in excess of a producer's annual allotment and is restricted from freely entering the market until released per Order provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salable carry-in reduces required salable quantity; reserve pool quantities provide a buffer for unexpected demand; Committee monitors both as indicators of excess supply and to determine appropriate salable quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer excess production transfers and reserve pool placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers who produce more than their annual allotments may transfer excess to producers who produced less. On December 1 each year, producers who have not transferred excess must place it into the reserve pool. Each producer controls disposition of their reserve pool oil subject to Order provisions and Committee oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers and reserve pool placement are part of volume regulation accounting and market supply management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing policy statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In conjunction with a recommendation for volume regulation, the Committee must prepare a marketing policy statement that meets the requirements of §§ 985.50 and 985.51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS reviewed the Committee's marketing policy statement for the 2025-2026 marketing year and found it meets statutory/regulatory requirements; marketing policy statements document the rationale and factors considered when recommending volume regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Regulatory Flexibility Act, AMS must analyze economic impacts of the proposed rule on small entities, including estimating number of producers/handlers that qualify as small entities using SBA size standards and considering alternatives and their impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule uses NASS price data, utilization, estimated handler markups, and SBA thresholds (e.g., $34 million for small agricultural service firms; $2.5 million for small agricultural producers) to estimate impacts and classify entities; calculations and estimates are provided showing most producers and all handlers qualify as small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order's information collection requirements have existing OMB approval (OMB No. 0581-0178) and the proposed rule does not impose additional reporting or recordkeeping requirements; any changes would be submitted to OMB for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS commits to reducing information requirements where possible and to comply with E-Government Act goals for public access; no new PRA burden is claimed for this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public meeting and outreach expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee meetings are public and widely publicized; the October 9, 2024 meeting was open to all interested persons who could attend and participate in deliberations on the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder input at production area meetings and the Committee meeting informed trade demand estimates and recommendations; the rule invites written comments in addition to public meeting participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific salable quantities and allotment percentages proposed
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2025-2026 marketing year beginning June 1, 2025: Class 1 (Scotch) oil — salable quantity of 808,656 pounds and allotment percentage of 35 percent; Class 3 (Native) oil — salable quantity of 1,028,670 pounds and allotment percentage of 39 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric values are adopted into the proposed regulatory text (§ 985.235) and form the basis for individual producer allotments when multiplied by each producer's allotment base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives considered and rationale for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee considered alternatives including no volume regulation and various salable quantities/allotment percentages above and below the recommended levels. No regulation was rejected because of likely severe, price-depressing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee analysis concluded volume regulation better prevents excessive stock buildups and price volatility; discussion of alternatives is part of the administrative record supporting the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data elements and computational inputs for supply-demand balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee calculations rely on estimated carry-in, estimated trade demand, computed minimum salable quantity (demand minus carry-in), total estimated allotment base, computed allotment percentage (minimum salable / allotment base), and recommended allotment percentage. Additional inputs include historical sales, production estimates, acreage changes, reserve pool amounts, and international market competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble provides itemized computational steps (A)-(H) for each class with numerical examples; total available supply is computed as recommended salable quantity plus carry-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Econometric modeling and price stability metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS used an econometric model to estimate market effects of volume regulation, including a projected season average producer price decline of about $2.78 per pound without volume regulation and use of coefficient of variation (CV) to measure price variability (24 percent with Order in effect vs. 49 percent pre-Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model outputs and CV comparisons are used to justify the price-stabilizing impact of the Order and support the recommendation for volume regulation.
